name: What if I hate the kitchen design after the first draft but feel bad asking for changes?

mainEntity.name: What if I hate the kitchen design after the first draft but feel bad asking for changes?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you dislike the first design, explain the specific problem rather than approving it to keep the project moving. Identify whether the issue is circulation, storage, appliance access, style, cost, or maintenance, then ask for a revised option before materials are ordered. Elite Remodeling & Design’s planning process can incorporate layout development, visualization, and selections before construction. Key factors include whether the change affects plumbing, electrical, structural work, cabinet orders, or permit documents. Mark up the plan and rank your must-haves. A small revision early is usually easier to manage than a field change after demolition or fabrication.
acceptedAnswer.description: Raise the concern before approvals and material orders. Describe the exact issue—traffic, storage, cost, appliance access, or style—mark it on the plan, and rank your must-haves so the design can be revised before construction creates expensive changes.
